extracted.intended_audience: PD/PIs, research administrators, and grant recipients preparing/submitting NIH RPPRs (Research Performance Progress Reports)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for completing NIH Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPR), including how to report publications, products, data management and sharing, participants, effort, changes, and special award-specific reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report publications that fall under NIH Public Access Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that fall under the NIH Public Access Policy (NOT-OD-25-047) and are non-compliant must be reported. NIH recipients are responsible for public access compliance of all the publications listed in section C.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliant publications must be reported; bringing publications into compliance typically takes weeks so PD/PIs are advised to act promptly. See Manage Compliance with the NIH Public Access Policy in My NCBI and NIH Public Access website for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not list papers for which award only provided non-personnel resources in C.1
rubrics_metrics.description: When an award’s only contribution to a publication is non-personnel resources (e.g., materials, equipment, data), applicants should not list the paper in section C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These papers may be listed in Section B.2 (description of accomplishments) but will not count against B.2's two-page limit and will not be tracked as a product of the award; the recipient is not responsible for ensuring these publications' public access compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use My NCBI publication tables and Associate with this RPPR checkbox correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR draws publication information from the PD/PI’s My NCBI account into three tables: All Publications Associated with this Project; Publications Not Associated with this Project; Publications Previously Reported for this Project. The 'Associate with this RPPR' box is automatically checked in the first table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving the box checked upon submission associates the publication with the progress report, displays it in RePORTER, and makes the award-publication association permanent in My NCBI/PubMed. Unchecking disassociates it and, upon submission, removes the award-publication association in My NCBI. Publication data is dynamic until report submission and is frozen upon submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report previously reported publications and ensure ongoing public access compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publications Previously Reported table lists publications reported in prior electronic progress reports; recipients are responsible for ensuring these publications comply with the Public Access policy even if listed as 'in Process' previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor compliance status and take corrective actions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report non-compliant publications and respond to automated notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: When non-compliant papers are reported, the system sends an automated email to the PD/PI (cc AO and SO) requesting evidence of compliance or an explanation by a specified due date (two weeks prior to next budget start date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond via email to GMS and PO or via PRAM link in eRA Commons. Provide My NCBI PDF report as simplest evidence and attach via PRAM. NIH will accept only compliance except in extremely rare circumstances (e.g., death of sole author).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PubMed Central submission instructions to bring publications into compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring a publication into compliance, follow PubMed Central submission instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/about/submission-methods/ for methods; use My NCBI PDF reports and PRAM for communicating compliance to NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Internet sites (C.2) with URL and short description when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: List the URL for any internet site that disseminates research results and provide a short description of each site. A description is required only for awards designed to create or maintain websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include publications already specified above. Limit responses to this reporting period. If award not designed to create/maintain websites, select Nothing to Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report technologies or techniques (C.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify technologies or techniques that have resulted from the research activities. Describe the technologies/techniques and how they are being shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PIs are required to report all technologies/techniques arising from the award. Use 'New Technology/Technique' button and select applicable product categories. Limit responses to this reporting period, and select 'Nothing to Report' if none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report inventions, patent applications and/or licenses (C.4) and prior reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if inventions, patent applications, and/or licenses resulted from the award during the reporting period and whether this information was previously provided to the PHS or official responsible for patent matters at the grantee organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting of inventions through iEdison is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Other Products (C.5.a) and assign product categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any other significant products developed under the project; PD/PIs must report all products that arise from their NIH award in section C, excluding SBIR/STTR commercial technologies (addressed under Impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click New Product and choose applicable product categories (1–14). If more than one product, add additional entries. Limit response to this reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product categorization (C.5) — use the specified list
rubrics_metrics.description: Products must be assigned to categories such as Audio/Video, Data/Databases, Research Material, Educational aids, Evaluation Instruments, Instruments/equipment, Models, Physical collections, Protocols, Software, Survey Instruments, Interventions, New Business Creation, Other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select as many categories as applicable. If product has been reported/shared through a publication include full reference and/or PubMed ID in the product description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim research products reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim research products are complete, public research products that are not final. Do not report interim versions unless they are complete drafts and public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations for interim products must include DOI and object type (e.g., preprint, protocol), version information (e.g., most recent date modified), and date the product was cited. Example citation format provided. For a draft to be listed as interim product it must be publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to claim interim research product as NIH award product
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim an interim research product as a product of an NIH award, the NIH expects the recipient will: make the product publicly available; in the text of the document acknowledge NIH funding, clearly state the work is not peer-reviewed, and declare any competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH strongly encourages a CC-BY license or dedication to public domain to maximize impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing expectations (C.5.b)
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs and recipient organizations are expected to make results and accomplishments available to the research community and public. If the initial research plan or award terms require a formal sharing plan, describe progress in implementing that plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For model organisms include number of requests received and fulfilled. If sharing plan fully implemented provide a final statement. NIH recipients subject to 2023 DMS Policy should report DMS activities in C.5.c and only report Resource Sharing in C.5.b when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing reporting (C.5.c) — applicability and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Question C.5.c applies only to NIH recipients subject to the 2023 NIH Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Policy; the system will auto-indicate applicability. Describe activities related to the approved DMS Plan for each Data Type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each Data Type provide: Data Type; Has data been generated to date? (Y/N); Has data been shared? (Y/N); if not shared, status (e.g., being prepared, submitted to repository, not yet expected); Repository; Unique Identifiers/DOI. If data not generated/shared as outlined, describe why and corrective actions. Use 'Add DMSP Information' for each Data Type and limit responses to reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting significant prospective changes to the DMS Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether significant prospective changes to the DMS Plan are being requested for the coming year (e.g., change in repository, timeline, scientific direction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 'No Change' if none. If Yes, enter description of changes, include effective date, rationale, justification, and describe impact on budget for coming and future periods. Upload revised DMS Plan as PDF named 'DMS Plan Revision'. Note: This is not a supplement request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report individuals who worked on the project (Section D.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide/update information for individuals who worked during the reporting period or may work in upcoming period: PDs/PIs; each person who worked at least one person month per year regardless of source of compensation; and all individuals required to submit a Biographical Sketch Common Form and/or Current and Pending (Other) Support Common Form (new Senior/Key, Senior/Key with changes, new Other Significant Contributors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not report personnel with PHS 2271 submitted through xTrain, existing Other Significant Contributors, or existing personnel (other than PD/PI) who worked less than 1.0 person month. For Final/Interim RPPRs report only individuals who worked in the last budget period minus approved no-cost extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual certification for MFTRP for senior/key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals serving as senior/key personnel must certify annually to their participation or non-participation in a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program (MFTRP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NOT-OD-26-018 for due dates and details; certification language must align with Common Forms. For RPPRs on/after Jan 25, 2026 upload a flattened PDF named 'MFTRPcert_[Name].pdf' with the required statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identification fields and use of Commons ID and ORCID
rubrics_metrics.description: Required fields are marked with *. Entering eRA Commons User ID allows 'Populate from Profile' to partially populate information. Commons ID is required for all Senior/Key Personnel, all individuals with a postdoctoral/graduate/undergraduate role, and all individuals required to provide Biographical Sketch/Current and Pending forms. Provide ORCID and ensure it aligns with ORCID linked to eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other project personnel with established Commons ID provide it. Use SciENcv for required forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Role and how to present role
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the role the person played on the project; this should be the most senior role in which the person worked for any significant length of time (e.g., a person who progressed from undergraduate to graduate should be shown as graduate student).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select role from dropdown list (Co-Investigator, Faculty, Postdoctoral Scholar, Technician, Staff Scientist, Statistician, Graduate Student, Non-Student Research Assistant, Undergraduate Student, High School Student, Consultant, Other). For Other Significant Contributors new to project, select 'Other' and specify 'OSC'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person months (effort) reporting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Person month equals approximately 160 hours (~8.3% annualized effort) and effort is based on type of appointment and organization's definition of appointment period. Effort for each individual in D.1 is retrospective for the prior reporting period and should be 1.0 or greater and rounded to nearest one-tenth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (1) PD/PI effort between 0.1 and 12.0 (round up to 0.1 if <0.05); cannot be zero unless policy allows; (2) persons who worked at least 1.0 person month — effort between 1.0 and 12.0 and cannot be zero; (3) New Senior/Key Personnel — effort between 0.1 and 12.0 (rounding rules apply) unless being added/promoted during next period then effort can be 0.0; (4) Senior/Key with changes in Current & Pending — effort between 1.0 and 12.0 and cannot be zero; (5) New Other Significant Contributors — effort entered as 0.0. See FAQs for calculating person months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Senior/Key Personnel and Other Significant Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior/Key Personnel are PD/PI and other individuals identified by recipient organization as contributing to scientific development/execution in a substantive, measurable way (typically doctoral/professional degrees but can include masters/baccalaureate or consultants/postdocs if they meet definition). Other Significant Contributors are not senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine who requires biosketches, current & pending forms, and effort reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for new Senior/Key Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Senior/Key Person is new to the project or elevated to Senior/Key role, upload a Biographical Sketch Common Form/NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement, Current and Pending (Other) Support Common Form and Supplemental Documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit documentation using SciENcv forms and follow SciENcv instructions and FAQs on Common Forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for changes in Current and Pending (Other) Support
rubrics_metrics.description: If there has been a change in active Current and Pending support of a Senior/Key Person since last reporting period, upload updated Current and Pending (Other) Support and supplemental documentation (as needed), listing the project for which the progress report is submitted and the effort to be devoted in the next reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SciENcv required forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for new Other Significant Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: If participant is a new Other Significant Contributor, upload a Biographical Sketch Common Form/NIH Biographical Sketch Supplement for this individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SciENcv forms; Other Significant Contributors commit to contribute but do not commit specified measurable effort (person months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report foreign primary affiliation properly
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual’s primary affiliation is with a foreign organization, indicate Yes/No. Check No if individual’s primary affiliation is foreign but the individual is working on this award solely while in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Yes, provide name of organization and country and add participant to table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report reductions in level of effort (D.2.a) and prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Will there be, in the next budget period, a reduction of 25% or more in level of effort from what was approved by the agency for PD/PI(s) or other senior/key personnel, or a reduction below the minimum required by the Notice of Award?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductions are cumulative across successive reductions. Selecting Yes constitutes a prior approval request; issuance of subsequent year of funding constitutes approval. Once agency approval is given for a significant change, subsequent reductions are measured against the approved adjusted level.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPI Leadership Plan changes (D.2.e) — when to report and approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Report if there will be a change in the MPI Leadership Plan for the next budget period. Change in status of PD/PI requires prior approval per NIH Grants Policy Statement; revision of Leadership Plan during project period may be accomplished by joint decision of PD/PIs and reported in RPPR; prior approval of a revision is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If yes, upload revised MPI Leadership Plan describing changes, including communication plans, procedures for resolving conflicts, and changes to responsibilities. Requests to change from multiple PD/PI to single PD/PI or to change number/makeup of PD/PIs require prior approval of GMO and cannot be requested via RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe impact on infrastructure resources (Section E.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe ways the project has impacted or is likely to impact physical, institutional, or information resources forming infrastructure (e.g., facilities, labs, instruments; establishment/sustenance of societies/organizations; information resources/electronic means for access or scientific communication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If award not intended to support such resources, select Nothing to Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report foreign expenditure amounts (E.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the dollar amount of the award’s budget being spent in foreign country(ies): for domestic recipients provide dollars obligated to first-tier subawards to foreign entities for this reporting period; for foreign recipients provide dollar amount of the award excluding first-tier subawards to U.S. entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dollars should reflect total costs. If more than one foreign country, identify distribution by country. Report only cumulative first-tier subaward dollars by country. Do not report foreign travel or purchases unless part of a first-tier subaward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report significant challenges or delays and corrective actions (F.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe actual or anticipated significant challenges or delays encountered during the reporting period and the actions or plans to resolve them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe only significant challenges that may impede the research (e.g., patient accrual, hiring, need for resources) and emphasize their resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report significant changes to human subjects, animals, biohazards, select agents (F.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe significant deviations, unexpected outcomes, or changes in approved protocols for human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes to human subjects provide description and include new/revised Protection of Human Subjects and Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children sections as in competing application instructions; update inclusion enrollment reports via Human Subjects System (HSS) as needed. For vertebrate animals provide description and examples of significant changes (e.g., changing species, new invasive procedures, new sites); for biohazards and select agents provide description and explanation of differences and regulatory status; include Select Agent Registry link for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address award-specific Special Reporting Requirements (Section G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address any special reporting requirements specified in the award terms and conditions in the Notice of Award (NoA) or Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: MFTRP certification upload for senior/key personnel; NRSA training award childcare usage attachment; SBIR/STTR Life Cycle Certifications required in Interim/Final RPPR and must be uploaded; SBIR/STTR Foreign Disclosure and Required Disclosures of Foreign Affiliations must be addressed as part of Annual/Interim/Final RPPR. Follow links and form locations provided.
